articles.title: Jason Voorhees Makes His Animated Debut in New ‘Never Hike Alone’ Short
articles.summary: More than 46 years after his big-screen debut in the slasher classic “Friday the 13th,” hulking horror icon Jason Voorhees is about to prove that his machete cuts just as deep in animation.
body: Founded in 2016 by filmmaker Vincente DiSanti, Womp Stomp Films has built a devoted following with its ambitious series of “Friday the 13th” fan films. The saga began with DiSanti’s 2017 short “Never Hike Alone,” followed by the winter-set prequel “Never Hike in the Snow” in 2020. The feature-length sequel “Never Hike Alone 2” arrived in 2023, featuring “Friday the 13th Part VI: Jason Lives” actors Thom Mathews and Vincent Guastaferro reprising their original roles as Tommy Jarvis and Sheriff Rick Cologne.

The “Never Hike Alone” films have relied on crowdfunding campaigns to help finance their increasingly elaborate productions. The fan-supported approach has allowed DiSanti and his collaborators to expand the saga while making the finished films available to watch for free online.

articles.title: Trump Hasn’t Commented on Nationwide Flight Shutdown, But He’s Promoting the Federal Film Incentive
articles.summary: As flights across the U.S. ground to a halt Friday amid a rare nationwide ground stop, President Donald Trump was focused on proclaiming his support for a federal film and television tax incentive.
body: The President has not yet issued a statement on the massive ground stop, which has delayed over 10,000 flights so far.

Instead Trump, who was perhaps responding to a Friday Politico article saying “Hollywood’s tax credit push runs into a post-midterm wall,” took to Truth Social to assure that, in a bipartison effort, “meetings are being set up to GET THIS DONE.”

articles.title: Seth Rogen on ‘The Invite,’ ‘Tangles,’ ‘The Studio’ Season 2, Reviving ‘Darkwing Duck’ and Why ‘Any A–hole Can Write That Joke’ Was the Best Advice He Ever Got
articles.summary: For years, people have told me that Seth Rogen and I are voice twins. Sitting across from him at the Middleburg Film Festival, deep in Virginia horse country, even Jeremy, the person recording our conversation, can confirm that the resemblance is very close.
body: In “The Invite,” Olivia Wilde’s A24 dinner-party indie, Rogen plays Joe, a husband whose fraying marriage gets stress-tested over one excruciating evening with the upstairs neighbors, played by Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton. I think it’s his finest hour as an actor. On paper, it sounds like a “another Seth Rogen” role. On screen, he plays it in a way we didn’t expect and he credits Wilde for taking his and Norton’s ideas to heart.
“She could have just not used any of it,” he says. “and I just would not have been as funny in it.”

On the episode of the Variety Awards Circuit Podcast, Rogen discusses his one-two punch of “The Invite” and “Tangles,” along with the recently announced “Darkwing Duck” revival at Disney+, the awards-season satire threaded through Season 2 of “The Studio” and how “Steve Jobs” opened a door to a part of the industry he had never been invited into. Listen below!

Among comedians, he says, going dramatic “almost feels like a bit of a cheat code” and he recalls Jonah Hill predicting “Moneyball” (2011) would bring him the most acclaim of his career for doing the least (Hill was right, getting his first Oscar nom for supporting actor).

articles.summary: JB Smoove brought his signature creative swagger and Evan Shapiro broke down the digital entertainment economy during lively conversations held as part of Variety‘s annual Business Managers Breakfast presented by City National Bank.
body: City National Bank president and CEO Howard Hammond kicked off the morning.
“You’re a core part of the past of City National Bank,” he told the SRO crowd of business managers. “But more importantly, our future will always be intertwined with entertainment and sports.”

He thanked attendees for their support as clients and “blunt feedback,” and recalled a conversation where Arnie Herrmann said the two things that made his career what it is today were trust and service.
The actor, comedian and entrepreneur sat down with Variety executive editor for television Michael Schneider, where he emphasized the importance of taking control.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson reportedly leads James Bond contenders
articles.summary: Reports that the star – the most high-profile of the final five contenders – has been offered favourable contract terms hint that Amazon MGM may want him as its first 007.
body: Robert Pattinson has emerged as the favourite in the race to succeed Daniel Craig as James Bond, according to a credible film-industry source.

Writing in Puck, Matthew Belloni suggests that the favourable contract terms he says have been offered to Pattinson suggest that the actor, currently in cinemas with reality-crime thriller Primetime, is studio Amazon MGM’s preferred choice for the role.
According to Belloni, while other actors on the shortlist were required to commit to four Bond films, Pattinson’s contract called for three – and offered a much larger (unspecified) fee.
According to Belloni, “it suggests the studio is willing or even eager to sacrifice a bit to get a ‘name’ star to front its most important franchise”.

articles.summary: The TV star fell victim to a practical joke from the Hollywood stars of the Dune franchise.
body: Timothée Chalamet and his Dune co-stars were seen pranking Rylan Clark during this year's Children in Need on Friday.

The Oscar-nominated actor was set up with behind-the-scenes suggestions in an Impractical Jokers-style set-up during an interview with Zendaya, Jason Momoa and Anya Taylor-Joy about the third instalment of the film franchise.

articles.title: Dept Q crew member dies after being injured at Edinburgh film studio
articles.summary: Emergency crews were called to reports of an incident at FirstStage in Leith.
body: A member of the crew for the Netflix series Dept Q has died after being seriously injured at a film studio in Edinburgh.
Emergency crews were called to FirstStage studio in Leith at about 15:00 on Thursday and the man was pronounced dead a short time later.
Left Bank Pictures, which is involved in making Dept Q, later said it was "shocked and saddened" by the death of a crew member.
Police Scotland said the death was not being treated as suspicious but inquiries into the circumstances were ongoing. The Health and Safety Executive said it was "aware" of the incident.

articles.title: Trump Says Federal Film Tax Credit Is Gaining Momentum
articles.summary: The proposal for film and TV tax incentives, which drew broad bipartisan support when it was introduced earlier this year, faces an uphill battle for passage in the lame-duck session.
body: After a sweeping loss at the midterms for Republicans dimmed the short-term prospects of a federal film and TV tax credit, President Trump is pushing for passage of legislation for production subsidies.
Trump on Friday said he’s working with lawmakers on both sides of the aisle on the legislation.
“The support and popularity of doing this, and bringing Entertainment back to the United States of America, has been unbelievable!” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

A bipartisan group of lawmakers has introduced proposed legislation to establish a federal film and TV tax credit, aimed at reshoring production to the U.S. amid a tit-for-tat battle among countries to host Hollywood.

articles.title: Ben Stiller Gives Update on His New York Knicks Documentary: “The Pressure Is on”
articles.summary: The actor tells The Hollywood Reporter that the multi-part doc, in development with HBO and A24, will explore the team's history and championship run.
body: Ben Stiller is sharing an update on his forthcoming New York Knicks documentary, and after the team’s historic championship earlier this year, he knows “the pressure is on.”

While premiering his next film, Focker-in-Law, slated for a Thanksgiving release, on Wednesday night in New York, Stiller teased the documentary to The Hollywood Reporter, describing it as a multi-part project exploring the Knicks’ history.

“It’s been fun to work on so far,” Stiller added, acknowledging the high expectations surrounding the project, especially after the Knicks won their first NBA championship since 1973 on June 13. The documentary was announced shortly afterward, with Stiller directing the project and following the team’s full arc from the ’90s to its record-breaking championship run this year.
“I feel like Knicks fans really love the Knicks, so the pressure is on to make something that lives up to what they want, but I hope it does,” Stiller said.

articles.title: Catherine Zeta-Jones says US move humbled her before big break with Steven Spielberg
articles.summary: The Swansea-born star got her big break in The Mask of Zorro which cemented her place as an A-lister.
body: Catherine Zeta-Jones has said she had an ego check after moving to America in the 1990s.

The Swansea-born star had become a household name in the UK, but Hollywood quickly provided a reality check for the rising star and she was even asked by casting agents if she had any acting experience.
It was during her stint on CBS mini-series Titanic that she was seen by Steven Spielberg who suggested she go for a role in The Mask of Zorro which he was producing.
"Five days later I got the job, and three days after that, I was down there starting my sword-fighting lessons," she said.

articles.title: Producer Kevin J. Walsh Had Seen It All. Then ‘Being Heumann’ Came Along
articles.summary: The Oscar-nominated producer helped open doors for the disabled community on the set of Sian Heder's latest pic: "I'm as proud of what we did behind the scenes to redefine access as I am of the quality of this movie."
body: After all, the Boston-area native served in a variety of assistant roles for Scott Rudin, Steven Spielberg and Tommy Mottola before eventually spending more than five years running Ridley Scott ’s company, Scott Free. There, he shepherded a dozen pictures, four of them directed by Scott, including All the Money in the World (2017), The Last Duel (2021), House of Gucci (2021) and Napoleon (2023). In other words, he’s as battle-tested as they come.

“ When Sian first asked me, ‘Why do you want to do this?’ my answer truly was, “Because the movie fucking terrifies me,’” Walsh tells The Hollywood Reporter in support of Being Heumann’s Nov. 13 release on Apple TV.

In 1977, disabled rights activist Judy Heumann helped organize the landmark Section 504 Sit-in, a nationwide protest aimed at compelling HEW Secretary Joseph Califano to finally sign the long-delayed regulations implementing Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973. Heumann and her fellow disabled activists occupied federal buildings across the country for more than three weeks until Califano finally put pen to paper.
